speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; please describe the onset, any changes in size or appearance, and whether you have a fever or recent insect bites.

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis. The presence of an ulcerative leg lesion following an ant bite, combined with a history of immunosuppression from corticosteroid use for anterior uveitis and Crohn's disease, strongly suggests a parasitic infection. While I have a provisional diagnosis based on the clinical picture, I will request a biopsy for definitive confirmation.
